producer_report.summary: Added a first-in, first-out landing queue to the drain, with no rebase. `LandingQueue` is a pure struct (a ticket counter and a `VecDeque<u64>`) kept in the drain's shared `State`. A worker joins it in the `RunStep::Passed` arm of `attempts`, so the queue order is the order runs pass. The place is a `LandingSlot` drop guard stored in the same tuple as the passed job. Both land calls borrow that one slot, and it is released and waiters woken on every return or panic. Before the unchanged `Drain::land`, `await_head` waits until the worker is head. A worker that is not head prints `drain      <job> waits in the landing queue` once. A head, and so a lone worker, never waits or prints. `Drain::land`, `Steps::land`, the `landing` mutex, athena-core and the `Steps` trait are untouched. Tests are additions only, in a new `landing_queue_tests` module. Six are unit tests of the queue and the guard. Three drive two workers through `drain_concurrent` and assert one exact log: the head keeps its place across its two land calls; the worker that passed first lands first although it is item `a`; a failed head releases its place. I confirmed the three drain tests fail without the queue: with `await_head` made a no-op they logged `gate timed out` and lacked the wait line. I added a note to section 6 of async-drain.md and an Unreleased CHANGELOG entry, both saying queue order is pass order and that there is no rebase.

open_issues: crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs is in the brief's deliverables but not in the request's Files line, and I deliberately left it unedited, as the accepted plan says. Its fake is single-worker and adds no ordering coverage, and editing existing scaffolding would break the 'tests only add' criterion. The new tests are in drain.rs.

If a future change stopped a failed head from releasing its slot, test `a_failed_head_releases_its_place` would hang rather than fail at 5 s. `await_head` has no timeout by design, and the test's gates cap only the fake's own waits.
mistakes: I started the full `cargo test -p athena-cli` in the background before I knew I could not read its output, so I could not read per-test results from it. I ran the in-file drain tests and the complete `tests/drain.rs` integration suite separately, and the background run exited 0.
learnings: `std::sync::Mutex` is unfair, so the drain tests gate on the new 'waits in the landing queue' line rather than on who wins the `landing` lock.

With `read_ahead` 0 and two workers, `drain_concurrent` goes straight to `run_batches`. Two items with disjoint touches form one group and run side by side. The `Steps` fake needs `caps`, `queue`, `previous_rating`, `approve`, `read`, `run`, `land`, `rate`, `check_page` and `check_cap`; the other methods have defaults.
`attempts` runs the land section once per loop pass with `passed` already set. The `failures >= ATTEMPTS` check (2) is what makes two land calls, so holding the slot in `passed` serves both.

`await_head` has no timeout: a non-head waiter would wait forever if a head never left. The guard drop and `notify_all`, plus the 20 ms `pause`, are what prevent that. The tests cap only their own gates.
desires: A way to read the output of a background command from inside the working directory. I started the full `cargo test -p athena-cli` in the background and could only learn its exit code from the completion notice.
